item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 242306
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located about 150 miles offshore of southwestern Mexico, on
Hurricane Odalys, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
Baja California, and on Tropical Storm Nolo, located a few hundred
miles south of the Big Island of Hawaii.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure is expected to form in a couple of days to
the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Afterwards, environmental
conditions should be favorable for gradual development, and a
tropical depression is likely to form late this weekend or early
next week as the system moves slowly west-northwestward to
northwestward, parallel to the coast of southern and southwestern
Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
An area of low pressure could form about 1000 miles east-southeast
of the Hawaiian Islands over the weekend. Environmental conditions
could support some gradual development of this system, and a
tropical depression could form late this weekend or early next week.
The system is forecast to move generally northeastward, remaining
well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Evans/Pasch

--------------------

DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Odalys was located
near latitude 16.8 North, longitude 124.9 West. Odalys is moving
toward the east-northeast near 8 mph (13 km/h), and this general
motion should continue through tonight. A gradual turn toward the
northeast and north is expected on Friday and Saturday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some intensity fluctuations are possible during the next day 
or so, followed by weakening through the weekend.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 976 mb (28.82 inches).

item.title: Hurricane Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026 
716 
WTPZ41 KNHC 242034
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Odalys Discussion Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 PM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026
 
There are hints of a ragged eye feature in recent visible satellite 
images of Odalys. A 1735 UTC 89 GHz GMI image of the hurricane 
showed a mostly closed mid-level eyewall, although convection was a 
bit thin on the west side due to moderate westerly shear. The 
various UW-CIMSS objective satellite intensity estimates range from 
71-84 kt. The initial intensity is held at 80 kt, in best agreement 
with recent D-MINT and SATCON estimates.

Odalys is moving east-northeastward (060/7 kt) while being steered 
by a mid- to upper-level trough to its northwest. The models 
generally agree that the hurricane should gradually turn toward the 
northeast and north over the next couple of days. There was a 
westward shift in the guidance envelope through the first 2-3 days 
of the forecast, and the NHC prediction was adjusted accordingly. 
The long-range track forecast is challenging, with Odalys forecast 
to become increasingly shallow while weakening and also possibly 
being influenced by the outer circulation of Hurricane Polo. The 
model spread greatly increases at 72-120 h, but the general signal 
is for a slower forward speed and a southward component of motion at 
days 3-5. The NHC forecast was nudged west of the previous one at 
these times, falling in between the latest TVCN and HCCA aids.

In the near term, small intensity fluctuations are possible as the 
improved structure of Odalys could allow for a little strengthening 
despite moderate shear and the potential for intrusion of drier air 
from the west. The latest intensity guidance shows little change 
during this period, and the NHC forecast follows suit. After 36 h, 
a faster rate of weakening is forecast based on an expected 
increase in shear, as well as decreasing SSTs along the forecast 
track. These conditions will likely make it difficult for Odalys to 
sustain organized convection later this weekend, and the updated 
forecast shows Odalys as a post-tropical cyclone at 72 h based on 
the latest GFS and ECMWF simulated satellite imagery.
 
Moisture from both Odalys and Polo will be carried a long distance 
into the southwestern U.S. this weekend and early next week, and may 
indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash flood threat in 
the region. See products issued by the Weather Prediction Center for 
more information.

item.title: Hurricane Polo Public Advisory Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Thu Sep 24 2026 
548 
WTPZ32 KNHC 250247
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Advisory Number  18
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 PM MST Thu Sep 24 2026
 
...POLO EXPECTED TO REGAIN CATEGORY 5 STATUS ON FRIDAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.1N 106.5W
ABOUT 195 MI...315 KM SW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 455 MI...735 KM SSE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...150 MPH...240 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...935 MB...27.61 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in Baja California Sur should monitor the progress of this
system.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located
near latitude 17.1 North, longitude 106.5 West.  Polo is moving
toward the west near 12 mph (19 km/h) and this motion is expected to
continue through Friday, followed by a west-northwestward to 
northwestward motion on Saturday.  On the forecast track, the core 
of Polo will continue to move away from the coast of southwestern 
Mexico overnight.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 150 mph (240 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Polo is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  Some strengthening is possible overnight, 
and Polo could become a category 5 hurricane again on Friday.  
Gradual weakening is forecast to occur starting Friday night and
Saturday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 935 mb (27.61 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Wind gusts to tropical-storm force are possible along
portions of the coast of southwestern Mexico for the next few hours.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce additional rainfall totals of 
2 to 4 inches across coastal portions of the Mexican states of 
Michoacan, Colima, northern and southern Jalisco, and Nayarit. This 
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, 
especially in areas of steep terrain. Additional rainfall of 1 to 2 
inches is possible in coastal portions of the Mexican states of 
central Jalisco and Guerrero.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will affect portions of the coast of
southwestern Mexico during the next couple of days. Swells will
spread northward along the coast of west-central Mexico and toward
Baja California Sur on Friday and into the weekend. These swells are
likely to cause life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal
flooding. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Thu Sep 24 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 250248
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  18
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 PM MST Thu Sep 24 2026

Powerful Polo continues to have an impressive presentation on 
satellite imagery.  The eye is estimated to be around 20 n mi in 
diameter and is embedded within a 180 n mi wide Central Dense 
Overcast of very cold cloud tops.  The upper-level outflow 
pattern is quite symmetrical, indicative of weak vertical wind shear 
over the system.  The advisory intensity is held at 130 kt, in 
reasonable agreement with a subjective Dvorak estimate from TAFB and 
objective estimates from UW-CIMSS.

The hurricane is now moving on a mainly westward track with an 
initial motion estimated to be about 280/9 kt.  There is little 
change to the track forecast philosophy from the previous advisory. 
Polo is currently being steered by the flow on the south 
side of a well-defined mid-tropospheric ridge that is building 
westward over northern Mexico.  This steering regime should 
continue through Friday.  After that, a mid-latitude trough moving 
eastward across the northeastern Pacific should prevent the ridge 
from building farther west, with Polo likely to recurve northward 
and northeastward around the western periphery of the ridge.  The 
track guidance is generally in agreement on this scenario, although 
there are still notable differences in forward speed among the 
models in the 3-5 day time frame.  The official forecast is similar 
to the previous one, aside from showing a bit wider turn around the 
ridge before nearing the Baja California Peninsula in around 96 
hours.  This is a blend of the latest GDMI and HCCA solutions.

Polo will continue to move over very warm waters and in a low 
vertical wind shear environment through Friday.  Given the conducive 
conditions, the hurricane could regain category 5 intensity soon.  
Around 36 hours, a gradual weakening trend is expected to begin due 
to some increase in shear.  The official intensity forecast is on 
the high side of the model guidance, and shows the system still 
near major hurricane strength while it approaches the Baja 
California peninsula.  Rapid weakening is expected when the cyclone 
crosses the peninsula and moves into mainland Mexico.
 
It should be noted that moisture from Hurricane Polo and Odalys
will be carried a long distance into the southwestern United States
this weekend and early next week, and may indirectly contribute to
a heavy rainfall and flash flood threat in the region. See products
issued by the Weather Prediction Center for more information.
 
 
Key Messages:

1. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact coastal portions 
of southwest Mexico through the evening.  This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.
 
2. Wind gusts to tropical storm force may still occur along 
portions of the southwestern coast of Mexico this evening.
 
3. Polo is forecast to approach the Baja California Peninsula early
next week as a hurricane.  Interests there should closely monitor
the latest updates and ensure that they have their preparedness
plan in place.
